title: Agrobacterium Mediated Transformation of Mimulus guttatus from Leaf Petiole Explants
author: Srinidhi Holalu
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8vghw3w

steps.title: Collect mature seeds
steps.instruction: Collect mature seeds from greenhouse or growth‑chamber grown Mimulus guttatus plants (avoid field‑collected seeds to reduce contamination).

steps.title: Surface‑sterilize seeds
steps.instruction: Place seeds in 1.5 mL sterilized Eppendorf tube(s), add 5 % bleach solution with a drop of hand‑soap, and shake vigorously for 8–10 minutes.

steps.title: Rinse seeds
steps.instruction: In a laminar‑flow hood discard the bleach solution, add sterile water, shake at least 30 seconds, repeat 5–6 times, then add ≥1 mL sterile water for later plating.

steps.title: Cold‑stratify seeds
steps.instruction: Store the rinsed seeds at 4 °C for 2–3 weeks.

steps.title: Plate seeds on growth medium
steps.instruction: Transfer sterilized seeds onto solid growth medium, spread uniformly, and place 5–6 seeds per 200 mL jar or quart‑size polypropylene Deli jar.

steps.title: Incubate seed cultures
steps.instruction: Incubate the jars at 20–21 °C under cool fluorescent lamps.

steps.title: Subculture proliferating shoots
steps.instruction: When axillary shoots proliferate, harvest shoots with roots and transfer to a fresh jar; adjust sub‑culture frequency to avoid senescence.

steps.title: Prepare Agrobacterium plate
steps.instruction: Streak EHA105 strain carrying the binary plasmid on LB or YEP agar containing rifampicin 40 µg mL⁻¹ and the plasmid’s selectable antibiotic; incubate 28 °C for 2 days.

steps.title: Inoculate liquid Agrobacterium culture
steps.instruction: Pick a single colony and inoculate into 10 mL YEP broth with rifampicin 40 µg mL⁻¹ and either kanamycin 50 µg mL⁻¹, spectinomycin 100 µg mL⁻¹, or ampicillin 100 µg mL⁻¹; shake at 28 °C, 200 rpm for 36–48 h.

steps.title: Induce virulence
steps.instruction: Centrifuge cultures at 4000 rpm, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 5 mL virulence‑induction medium, adjust pH to 5.5, and incubate 3.5–4 h with gentle shaking (50–80 rpm) in the dark at room temperature; glucose may replace sucrose but use sucrose for older leaves.

steps.title: Adjust Agrobacterium density
steps.instruction: Dilute the induced culture with half‑strength MS medium to an optical density (OD₆₀₀) of 0.2, producing a very light‑colored suspension; higher OD is undesirable.

steps.title: Prepare leaf petiole explants
steps.instruction: In the hood, pull shoots onto a sterile Petri dish, cut a leaf explant with a sterile scalpel, dip the cut petiole into the OD‑0.2 Agrobacterium suspension, and place on co‑cultivation medium; work in small batches to prevent desiccation.

steps.title: Co‑cultivate explants
steps.instruction: Incubate the plates in darkness or low‑intensity light at room temperature for 2–3 days, monitoring for Agrobacterium overgrowth.

steps.title: Wash and select explants
steps.instruction: On day 3, wash explants in sterile timentin 100 mg L⁻¹ + cefotaxime 50 mg L⁻¹, then transfer to callus‑induction medium containing phosphinothrocin (selection for Blp resistance); incubate at 21 °C under cool fluorescent lamps.

steps.title: Subculture callus
steps.instruction: After 21–24 days, retain a small portion of callus and transfer to fresh callus‑induction medium; repeat subculture every 21–24 days for at least 3–4 cycles, increasing sucrose to 2.5 % in later stages; avoid premature transfer to Meta‑toplin.

steps.title: Induce shoot regeneration
steps.instruction: When compact callus becomes friable and shows differentiation, pick healthy callus and plate on shoot‑induction medium to regenerate shoots.

steps.title: Root regenerated shoots
steps.instruction: When shoots reach 0.5–1 cm, separate individual shoots and place on rooting medium.

steps.title: Improve rooting and hardening
steps.instruction: Subculture shoots onto half‑strength rooting medium to enhance rooting and hardening.

steps.title: Acclimatize plantlets
steps.instruction: When roots have proliferated, transfer shoots to potting medium in the greenhouse and place pots on a mist bench for hardening for at least two weeks.
